ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass — SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96() returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder does not explicitly check for zero
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Code asymmetry confirmed: _validatePricingBounds (L847) checks sqrtPriceX96==0 but validateHandlerOrder (L215-223) does not. However, CLOB constrains sqrtPriceX96 to MIN_SQRT_RATIO..MAX_SQRT_RATIO and orderAmount to uint128.max, so computeRatioX96 never returns 0 for CLOB-constrained parameters. Forge tests prove no overflow path exists within CLOB bounds. When minSqrtPriceX96 is set, the min check catches sqrtPriceX96==0 anyway.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call — calling handler functions directly (not via AMM) to bypass pricing hooks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer checks msg.sender == AMM (L230). PermitTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer checks msg.sender == AMM (L115). Both revert with CallbackMustBeFromAMM. No executeSwap function exists. User-facing functions (openOrder, closeOrder, deposit, withdraw) have independent validation. Forge test confirms external callers are rejected.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — CLOBTransferHandler.setTokenSettings may leave stale memSettings in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Registry-hook desynchronization is documented and intentional (CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol L23-53). CLOBTransferHandler reads settings from AMM via ILimitBreakAMM(AMM).getTokenSettings() (L582-583), not from the registry directly. The initialized flag is always set to true on setTokenSettings (L377). Known Low severity (CP-005): gas waste only, no security impact.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT not cleared after afterSwap, stale data for next direct swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known issue HOOK-001/CP-001. Slot written in beforeSwap (L839), read in afterSwap (L843-844), never cleared. By-design: AMM calls beforeSwap per-token, second call overwrites first. Each direct swap writes fresh value before read. Cross-swap stale reads only if afterSwap runs without preceding beforeSwap, which AMM flow prevents. Forge test confirms reentrancy guard blocks re-entry and transient storage persists within tx but is overwritten by fresh beforeSwap.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Malicious pool type returns inflated amountOut to steal from LPs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool type is chosen by pool creator at creation. AMM trusts pool type return values for amountOut but decrements reserves with _safeDecrementUint128 (underflow guard). A malicious pool type can only drain its own pool's reserves — funds from LPs who chose that pool. This is the intended trust model. No cross-pool extraction. Pool type address must have 6 leading zero bytes.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: Malicious transfer handler skips actual transfer, core believes funds arrived
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: After handler execution, AMM checks balanceInBefore + swapCache.amountIn == balanceInAfter (AMMModule.sol:2208). If handler didn't transfer tokens, check fails with LBAMM__TokenInTransferFailed. Strict equality check — no tolerance for partial transfers.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: Malicious hook manipulates price limits to extract from swappers
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fees bounded by maxHookFee0/maxHookFee1 params set by pool creator. beforeSwap and afterSwap protected by _requireCallerIsAMM(). Hook cannot modify swap amounts directly — only return fee values which are capped. Forge test confirms external calls to hooks are rejected.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: Pool type address collision — deploy malicious contract at address matching legitimate type
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool type addresses must have 6 leading zero bytes (48-bit constraint via POOL_TYPE_ADDRESS_MASK). PoolId encodes pool type address. Collision requires deploying at EXACT same address (same deployer + CREATE2 salt). No pool type registry to poison — each pool stores its own type reference.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: UUPS/beacon takeover before initializer runs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: LimitBreakAMM uses SecureProxy (not UUPS/beacon). Proxy upgrade requires SECURE_PROXY_CODE_MANAGER_ROLE. Implementation is set via OwnablePermissions-based access control. No unguarded initializer — constructor sets immutable module addresses. No initialize() function to front-run.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Selector collision — deploy facet with colliding selector to hijack calls
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: LimitBreakAMM is NOT EIP-2535 diamond. It uses delegateCallPure modifier to route to immutable module addresses set in constructor. Module addresses cannot be changed post-deployment. Selector routing is hardcoded in the fallback/receive functions. No facet registry to inject selectors into.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7: CREATE2 destroy-redeploy — selfdestruct trusted address, redeploy malicious code
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SELFDESTRUCT is deprecated post-Dencun (EIP-6780). Only destroys in same tx as creation. Trusted addresses (modules, handlers) are deployed before use and immutable. Even pre-Dencun, redeploying at same CREATE2 address requires same init code, making malicious code injection impossible without changing the bytecode hash.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: SELFDESTRUCT deprecated post-Dencun, no redeployment attack path

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H8: Storage slot collision across diamond facets — malicious facet writes to another facet's slot
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All diamond facets (AMMModule, ModuleAdmin, ModuleFeeCollection, ModuleLiquidity) use 0 direct storage slots — all state via Storage.appStorage() at 0x9A1D. Slither storage layout confirms 0 slots for each. AMMStandardHook uses slots 0-4 but is a separate contract (not delegatecall target). No collision possible within the diamond.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H9: Exploit facet management to add malicious facet without governance
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No facet management system exists. Modules are immutable constructor parameters. SecureProxy upgrade requires SECURE_PROXY_CODE_MANAGER_ROLE. No addFacet/replaceFacet/removeFacet functions exist anywhere in the codebase.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction — run 100+ tiny swaps to leak value per iteration
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool type swap functions round in favor of protocol/pool. SqrtPriceMath rounds amounts up for input, down for output. Tiny swaps lose to rounding on each iteration. Cross-boundary test confirms no accumulation path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Permit mutation — replay signature with mutated unsigned fields (feeOnTop, recipient) to redirect funds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop intentionally unsigned (documented design). limitAmount in signed permit caps total exposure. Even with mutated feeOnTop, signer's maximum loss is bounded by limitAmount which they chose.

Compared beforeSwap vs afterSwap — both require _requireCallerIsAMM(). Compared _validatePricingBounds vs validateHandlerOrder — asymmetry found (KV-1) but not exploitable.
